subject: maths
question: A certain sum of money becomes 4 times in 12 years when invested at simple interest. In how many years will it become 10 times of itself at the same rate?
solution:
Given:

The principal amount becomes 4 times in 12 years when invested at simple interest.

Concept used:

Simple Interest, SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

where

P = Principal amount

R = Rate of interest per year

T = Time in years

Calculation:

Let the principal amount be Rs. P and the rate of interest be R%.

According to the question,

(P × R × 12)/100 = 4P - P

⇒ R = 25%

Let the time taken for the principal amount to be 10 times of itself be T.

According to the question,

(P × 25 × T)/100 = 10P - P

⇒ T = 36

**∴ In 36 years the principal amount will become 10 times itself at the same rate. **
